title: Corrective Action Notices (CAN) & Corrective Action Plans (CAP)
subtitle: Closed-Loop CAN/CAP Workflow (FORM SMSM 8.8.2)
overview: A Corrective Action Notice (CAN) is issued against a hazard, finding, or report and assigns a required corrective action to an owner with a target completion date.

The owner responds with a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) that details the action plan, timeline, root-cause analysis, evidence, and sign-offs. The workflow stays open until the CAP is accepted and closed.

method.title: Method & Scoring Rules
paragraphs: CAN lifecycle — Open → Under Review → Closed (or Escalated). A CAN carries title, description, required action, assigned owner, department, priority and target date, plus the optional FORM SMSM 8.8.2 issuance block (copies to, requested/addressed function, initial 5x5 SRA).

CAP lifecycle — In Progress → Under Review → Completed, with Revision Required and Overdue states. Each CAP is linked to its CAN (can_id) and carries an action plan, timeline, resources and a target completion date.
Root-cause promotion — in the Combined RCA + SRAM workflow, 6M Fishbone root causes are promoted into Bow-Tie New Control Measures (NCM) and the SRAM data is persisted with the CAP.

Evidence & sign-off — the CAP mirrors FORM SMSM 8.8.2 Section 5.1 analysis items (factual review, RCA, short-term and long-term corrective actions, implementation timeline), plus managerial approval and CAA acceptance sign-off blocks, residual-risk 5x5 SRA, and closure details (closed_by, closed_signature, closed_at).
bullets: RCA block: root_causes [{ category, description, is_primary }] and action_items [{ description, root_cause_id, owner, target_date }].
145 / CAMO accounts can only create and review CAPs for their own department.
A CAP can be sent back with Revision Required and a new revision deadline instead of being closed.

mapping.title: CAR-19 / Appendix 10 Mapping
paragraphs: The closed-loop CAN/CAP process is ICAO Annex 19 Component 3 — Safety Assurance: monitoring of corrective actions, management of change, and continuous improvement.
It closes the loop opened by Component 2 (SRM) — each hazard/risk must end in an implemented, verified and signed-off corrective action.

example.title: Worked Example
paragraphs: Finding: debris (FOD) repeatedly observed on the apron near Gate 3.
CAN issued to Ground Operations: 'Implement and enforce daily FOD sweeps' — priority High, target 14 days.
CAP submitted: daily FOD sweep procedure with a checklist, sweep logs as evidence, and a short-term mitigation (pre-arrival walk) plus long-term fix (apron edge repair).
Root cause promoted: Method — 'no scheduled FOD sweep' becomes a New Control Measure in the Bow-Tie.
Sign-off: managerial approval → CAA acceptance → residual-risk SRA re-assessed → CAP closed with closure signature and timestamp.
